title: Capstone: does a list contain a duplicate?
idea: GUIDED CAPSTONE. The toughest list puzzle: compare every pair with a nested loop and a flag — all your tools woven together.
problem: Decide whether [4, 1, 7, 1] has any repeated value (yes — 1 appears twice).

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: does [4, 1, 7, 1] have a duplicate? OUTPUT is...
options: A yes/no (has a duplicate or not)
exercises.explanation: Output is a verdict. We check whether any value appears more than once.

exercises.prompt: To compare every value with every other, what structure do we need?
options: A loop inside a loop (nested loops)
exercises.explanation: A nested loop pairs each item with every other item. That's how we check all pairs.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand: comparing positions, which two positions hold equal values in [4, 1, 7, 1]?
exercises.explanation: Index 1 and index 3 both hold 1 — a duplicate. Found by comparing pairs.

exercises.prompt: We must avoid comparing an item with ITSELF (same position), or every item looks like a duplicate.
exercises.explanation: Right — compare position i with a LATER position j (j after i). That's why the inner loop starts past i.

blocks: For each later item j, if numbers[i] == numbers[j], set found True
exercises.explanation: Flag False; outer loop picks i, inner loop checks every j after i for an equal value. Nested-loop search.

exercises.prompt: To avoid self-comparison and double-checking, the inner loop should start at...
exercises.explanation: Starting at i+1 compares each pair once and never an item with itself. A deliberate index choice.

exercises.prompt: Code the inner comparison. Arrange the lines.
exercises.explanation: Inner loop over later positions, compare the two items, flip found on a match. Deep indentation marks the nesting.
== compares the two values. For [4,1,7,1], positions 1 and 3 match, so found becomes True.

exercises.prompt: Run it on [4, 1, 7, 1]: found is True. Hand said duplicate exists. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Matches. The nested loop found the repeated 1. You just used loops inside loops — the full toolkit!

exercises.prompt: Re-run on [4, 1, 7, 9] (all different). What does found end as?
exercises.explanation: No pair is equal, so found stays False. The 'no duplicate' case works. You've mastered nested-loop reasoning!
